title: 200 Volunteers, 1352 Meal Boxes, One Billings Morning - My 103.5
content: By 9:30 on this chilly Friday morning, folks from across the Billings area were already piling into the MetraPark carnival grounds. They arrived in cars, trucks, and school buses. And they weren't here for a concert, a trade show, or a rodeo. An estimated 200 people of all ages were there to help with Flakesgiving, Billings' annual Thanksgiving food drive. Founded nearly 40 years ago and led by Mark Wilson & Paul Mushaben, aka "The Breakfast Flakes," the event is a huge undertaking. Read More: Flakesgiving 2026: What You Need to Know Assembling 1,352 complete Thanksgiving meal kit boxes takes a lot of work. You know that old saying, "Many hands make light work"? This is a prime example. With Paul directing the operation, lines and job duties were assigned to all of the volunteers. Some helped with unboxing the bulk foods. Others were on trash duty, loading dumpsters with empty boxes. Others were stationed along the "assembly line", dropping a turkey, a bag of potatoes, canned goods, rice, and other items into each box, as another team then loaded them into the refrigerated truck. Each Flakesgiving box provides enough food for 10, which means 13,000 folks in Billings and the surrounding area will be able to enjoy a Thanksgiving meal this year at no cost. Loading the boxes is just a portion of the work. On Saturday, a fleet of volunteers will take the food boxes to seniors, invalids, and others in our community who lack transportation. Many of our volunteer drivers have been participating for years. I spoke with several youth who were helping load boxes on Friday about why they volunteered. Ellie and Madalyn are from Laurel High School. They said they like helping out people who might be struggling. They were both part of the National Honor Society. It was their first year participating in Flakesgiving. Cole Clark from Worden came out to help because his school's wrestling team was volunteering as well. Clark mentioned he's in 4-H, and volunteerism is something he can put in his record book, but "that's not the reason I do it", adding that it feels good to give back. Brent Scott, an advisor for the Laurel High School Honor Society, said, It's important for our kids to do service to their community, and it's one of the four pillars of the National Honor Society. This [Flakesgiving] is a great program that's been going on for years feeding hungry people in the community and so we love to be a part of it. They work at Grizzly Glass and said their job gave them time off from the shop to come volunteer as part of the company's community service initiatives. Several volunteers were spotted handing checks to Mark and Paul while I was there, and of course, these generous donations are what make Flakegiving possible. If you would like to donate to the Flakes Foundation — a 501(c)(3) organization — address your checks to Flakegiving and mail to: PO BOX 1276, Billings, MT, 59103. For those interested in receiving a Flakesgiving meal kit box, the line starts at noon in the carnival lot at MetraPark. No ID required, no questions asked, no proof of need necessary. One box per person, please. There are typically plenty of boxes available for those who arrive on Saturday, and any boxes that remain unclaimed are delivered to Family Service.

title: How Much Snow Does Cochise County Actually Get? - k101sv.com
content: Winter is right around the corner, and many Cochise County residents are wondering whether they'll see snow this year. While southeastern Arizona is better known for sunshine than snowstorms, winter weather remains a yearly occurrence across the region. From light dustings in the valleys to snow-covered mountain peaks, here's what to know about Cochise County's snowfall, winter conditions, and what the 2026-27 season may have in store! In Cochise County, elevation plays a huge role in your winter weather experience. At roughly 4,600 feet, Sierra Vista receives about 0.4 inches of snow a year on average, according to Current Results. Bisbee, the Coronado National Monument, and the Chiricahua National Monument all have an elevation above 5000 feet and receive an average of 3-4 inches of snow a year. The rest of the county rarely gets more than an inch and a half. While significant snowfall is uncommon outside of the mountains, even lower elevations of the county can expect to see at least a slight dusting of snow every year. READ: Top 3 Places To Visit In The Coronado National Forest. For a snowfront to hit the county, winter temperatures must fall below 32 degrees. Most snowfall occurs between December and February, although sometimes it will land in November or March if the conditions are right. In Sierra Vista and other valley communities, snow melts very quickly, rarely lasting a full day, unless there is shade. At higher elevations, snow can last several days, and in some cases more than a week! Because snow is infrequent and short-lived, it always creates a sense of excitement when it arrives. FUN FACT: Despite being an Arizona City, Flagstaff gets around 90 inches of snow annually, making it one of the snowiest cities in the country! In 2026, Cochise County experienced unusual weather compared to previous years. Between 2023 and 2025, the county only experienced an average of 10 inches of rain, while in 2026 some areas received more than 16 inches. With a wetter-than-average year, conditions may be more favorable for winter storms! While no forecast this early in the season can guarantee snowfall, The Old Farmer’s Almanac predicts a colder, wetter-than-normal winter driven by the El Niño weather patterns seen earlier in the year. Lower elevations will mostly see rain, but the surrounding mountain peaks have a high probability of receiving significant snowfall. READ: Coronado National Forest: Best Places to See Fall Colors! Winter in Cochise County may be brief, but it can still bring a touch of snow to the region each year. Whether it's a light dusting in Sierra Vista or a blanket of snow across the Huachuca and Chiricahua Mountains, winter weather always has a way of surprising residents. If forecasts hold true, this year's colder, wetter conditions could make those snowy moments a little more common. CONTINUE READING: How do Snowbirds Impact Cochise County?

title: New Place In St. George Might Be Serving Up The Area’s Best Orange Chicken - Cat Country 107.3 and 94.9
content: There is a restaurant that opened in St. George this fall that is serving up Asian food at a good price. It is the Hornbill Asian Cuisine and they have sushi and other dishes made for taking with you. They also have some exceptional orange chicken. This is easy to miss as it is on the backside of a row of businesses on the road that goes by Costco towards Deseret Industries. It offers Asian dishes and sushi in to go packaging that make it easy to pack up and go. The food is reasonably priced with classic rolls like the California roll for just $5.99 and specialty rolls like the Tempura Shrimp Roll at $8.49. That is a great price for restaurant quality sushi. The packaging made it feel like the sushi you see in the grocery store, but the rolls I ate were fresh and tasty. It is a good place to enjoy sushi that won't break your wallet. The Asian dishes I tried were even better. I tried the poke bowl which was good, but the orange chicken stood out. The chicken was cooked just right and it kind of melted a little in my mouth. The flavor was right on without the orange getting too heavy like sometimes happens. The rice it was on was also good and didn't need any extra sauce to eat it. This was the best orange chicken I have had in a long time. The reviews I read from people have visited Hornbill also liked the other Asian dishes on the menu. title: Cups & Cakes in Rumson, NJ makes everything fresh daily, from custom cakes and more - New Jersey 101.5
content: There's a difference between your typical local spot, and that local spot where everybody knows your name. And earlier this week, that's exactly what I experienced when I paid a visit to Cups & Cakes in Rumson, NJ. Just the setting alone paints the picture of a unique small town bakery where all the locals frequent. But to actually hear customers talk with the staff as if they were long time friends is rare. However, that kind of interaction is not rare in a place like Cups & Cakes. And it's exactly the kind of atmosphere Denise, the owner, set out for going back to 2010 when they first opened their doors. From the moment I walked in, Denise was deep in conversation with a customer that you would swear are good friends or family members. It was very refreshing to say the least. And that was before I even had a chance to meet Denise to check out her store. It was quite the first impression, and one that you'll notice immediately from the first time you walk through the doors. Denise and the crew take pride in serving the community and creating all the custom cakes, cookies, and desserts they're known for. But it's so much more than that. They've got breakfast sandwiches, a juice bar, coffees, just to mention a few. All of it is amazing and just as good as the desserts. Speaking of which, they make everything fresh, everyday. One thing that stood out to me was when Denise shared what they do with their leftover food. They freeze it and donate it to numerous local soup kitchens in the area. I absolutely love that and can see why Denise is so loved in the community. Cups & Cakes in Rumson is looking for your vote to help crown them the champion in this years Jersey Shore Dessert Wars. Fisher Asset Management, the firm behind Fisher Investments, reported a 13F portfolio worth about $348.3 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from roughly $335.8 billion three months earlier. The leading semiconductor foundry has fallen with the wider artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Shares are down roughly 26% since hitting an early-October peak of $487, pulled down by a semiconductor sell-off triggered by leadership turmoil at Nvidia (NVDA) and fresh U.S. export curbs. On the company's third-quarter earnings call in October, CEO C.C. Wei said, "demand for our leading-edge technologies continues to be extremely robust." The company's October 2026 revenue also grew 59.7% year-over-year. While AI spending could disappoint, and China restrictions carry real consequences, TSMC's customers still need more advanced manufacturing capacity than it can supply. At about 15.38x next year's earnings, I think the sell-off offers an attractive entry point. I therefore rate TSM stock a Buy. Get 75% Off TipRanks Premium and unlock powerful investing tools to make smarter, more confident investment decisions Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks AI fears have overshadowed TSMC's position, in my view. Investors are questioning whether hyperscalers will earn adequate returns on enormous infrastructure spending. Nvidia's leadership turmoil has intensified uncertainty around its China business. The announcement from Washington earlier this week adds tougher foundry-customer checks and restrictions targeting China's remote access to advanced AI computing. Those developments can remove potential orders. Nvidia is a major customer, and a broader spending slowdown would affect TSMC. Its customer diversity doesn't protect it from an industry-wide retrenchment. Rather, it provides exposure across competing chip designs. Nvidia could lose some accelerator share while AMD (AMD) gains it. Both companies rely on TSMC for advanced manufacturing. Google (GOOGL) and Amazon's (AMZN) custom accelerators provide other routes for AI spending to reach the foundry. Broadcom's (AVGO) designs are another example. Its latest quarterly filing says TSMC produced roughly 95% of wafers supplied by its contract manufacturers during the first nine months. So changing winners among chip designers needn't mean fewer orders for TSMC. That distinction is central to my thesis. Customers can compete fiercely over AI profits while continuing to buy manufacturing services from the same supplier. TSMC's process expertise makes switching difficult. Its enormous scale also helps spread development costs across a broad customer base. Building another leading-edge factory takes years, and matching its yields is a separate challenge. I think the market is applying too much of chip designers' uncertainty to the company that manufactures their products. TSMC's October revenue strengthens the growth case after an already excellent Q3. Quarterly revenue rose 50.9% in Taiwan dollars, while net income increased 68.7%. Gross margin reached 66.4%, and 2nm contributed 8% of wafer revenue. Then last week's monthly report showed record October revenue of NT$586.9 billion (about $17.8 billion). That was up 14.7% sequentially and 59.7% year-over-year. Revenue through October increased 43.3%. Growth accelerated after Q3, using the same local-currency comparison. That's difficult to reconcile with the idea that demand is already weakening materially. Management's Q4 revenue guidance of $52.3 billion–$54.3 billion comes with 65%–67% gross margins. The steep 2nm ramp should help. More revealing, though, is the spending commitment beyond this quarter. TSMC expects $60 billion–$64 billion of capex in 2026, and management indicated that total investment over 2026–2028 should significantly exceed the previous three years. Since leading-edge capacity takes years to bring online, customers plan capacity alongside TSMC well in advance. Management has even sent teams to check U.S. data center construction and power availability. Capex doesn't guarantee future sales, but collaborative capacity planning gives these investment figures far more weight than an optimistic forecast alone. The 2nm family's annual capacity should more than double in 2027. A16 expands its high-performance computing offering, while A14 volume production is planned for 2028. Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) packaging remains another scarce capability needed to assemble advanced AI systems. Agentic workloads are increasing demand for central processing units (CPUs), alongside inference accelerators and networking chips. Smartphones also support adoption of advanced processes. Overseas expansion, including Arizona's next fab in 2027, adds capacity across more locations. So I see a manufacturing franchise expanding around several sources of demand, with customers already planning subsequent product generations. TSMC's valuation leaves room for excellent returns if earnings follow current expectations. At today's price, consensus 2026 earnings per share (EPS) of $17.50 implies 20.55x earnings. The $23.39 estimate for 2027 reduces that to 15.38x. By 2028, $29.82 of EPS implies just 12.06x. Those forecasts assume roughly 34% earnings growth next year and 27.5% afterward. This is an unusually modest price for this growth profile. The opportunity has historical context. Forward P/E fell near 12x–13x in late 2022 and roughly 15x during parts of 2023. Patient buyers eventually benefited as earnings recovered and the shares rerated. I use that comparison cautiously. Still, today's business is growing rapidly, with October revenue 59.7% higher. The technology position remains strong, and new capacity is being planned against customer demand. That makes a compressed multiple particularly interesting to me. Customer concentration and Taiwan's geopolitical risks deserve a valuation discount. Export restrictions could tighten further, and enormous capex creates financial exposure if demand slows. Overseas fabs can also pressure margins. Eventually, leading-edge supply could catch up. Still, even 16x the 2028 EPS estimate would imply roughly $477 per share before dividends. That illustrates why the return case can work without an extreme valuation. Further estimate increases would provide additional upside. Taiwan Semiconductor stock has a Strong Buy consensus on TipRanks, based on nine unanimous Buy ratings. The average price target of $563.75 implies roughly 57% upside from today's price levels. Wall Street therefore remains optimistic despite the recent deterioration in semiconductor sentiment. TSMC will feel any genuine slowdown in AI investment. Yet its latest revenue figures show customers still demanding more leading-edge capacity. It can benefit as competing chip designers expand, even as market shares shift. At about 15.38x 2027 earnings, I think that position is attractively priced. October's revenue acceleration gives me more confidence in buying the decline. The rule amends the presumptions that front-end chip fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips, reducing the pathways to overcome them for chip designers located in destinations that face a license requirement. It also requires a license for advanced semiconductors sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
